html:
The Hirak was a wave of peaceful mass protests in Algeria that began on 22 February 2019, when President Abdelaziz Bouteflika, old and silent after a stroke, sought a fifth term.

Every Friday for months, millions marched in Algiers and other cities. On 2 April 2019 the army chief forced Bouteflika to resign after twenty years in power. The protesters kept marching against the military-backed system as a whole, and many boycotted the election of December 2019 that made Abdelmadjid Tebboune president.

The marches stopped during the COVID pandemic in 2020 and were later banned, and many activists were jailed. The Hirak broke the fear left by the civil war. Compare the Arab Spring of 2011, which Algeria had largely avoided.
sum: The Hirak was a wave of peaceful mass protests in Algeria that began on 22 February 2019, when President Abdelaziz Bouteflika, old and silent after a stroke, sought a fifth term.
